summary: Rename account_user.note to customer_note by adding the new column, backfilling data, creating a bidirectional database trigger to synchronize both columns during concurrent app operation, deploying the new version with a state-only migration, retiring the old version, and dropping the old column.
write_consistency: A database trigger synchronises note and customer_note on every INSERT/UPDATE from either app version, ensuring both columns always hold the same value and both app versions see the most recent write from either version.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed during stage expand because the PL/pgSQL trigger function body contained internal semicolons that the runner's executor misinterpreted as statement separators, causing a syntax error. This revision ensures each SQL string in the expand stage is a single valid PostgreSQL command with proper dollar-quoting ($$ ... $$) for the function body, and the trigger is created before deploy_new so synchronization is active before any concurrent traffic runs. The function body logic was simplified to a single-statement-per-branch structure that the runner's executor can process without splitting on semicolons, and the final SQL string terminator is correctly placed after the LANGUAGE clause.

stages.description: Add customer_note column, backfill from note, and create a trigger to keep note and customer_note in sync.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS customer_note TEXT;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; IF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; END IF; RETURN NEW; END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_customer_note AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Deploy the new version (new-staged) with a state-only Django migration. The new app only knows customer_note and will read/write that column.
Retire the old version. After this stage, only the new app serves traffic against the database.
Drop the sync trigger and the old note column now that the old app is retired.
sql: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS sync_note_customer_note ON account_user;
ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
